items.name: Readability
items.evidence: No files were saved. The agent ran throwaway inline `python3 -c` one-liners (XOR decrypt, then a sqlite3 json.dump) through task-exec, so there is no code to judge for readability.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: No code change was recorded. The work happened as ad-hoc shell/python one-liners and no script was persisted. It isn't re-runnable as the conventions ask, but there is no code here to grade on structure.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No code was saved. The one-liners had no error handling, but the agent checked each step manually (xxd header, integrity_check, count(*)=11). There is no artifact to grade.

items.name: Recovery method is principled
items.evidence: Derived the key from evidence: the header `75 3d 44 c0` is the magic `37 7f 06 82` XOR 0x42, and the runs of 0x42 are zeroed bytes. Decrypted the whole file and let SQLite replay the WAL. Verified with `PRAGMA integrity_check` → ok and `count(*)` = 11.

items.name: Original evidence preserved before in-place repair
items.name_zh: 原地修复前保留原始文件
items.evidence: Backed up first: `cp main.db-wal /tmp/wal.enc.bak && cp main.db /tmp/main.db.bak`, then decrypted in place and opened SQLite. The backups survived the WAL checkpoint/deletion, and the final message says where they are.
